text:
Aisha (Support): heads up — customer ACMEInc reported a big latency regression on our /v1/chat/tool-run endpoint after yesterday's runtime deploy. p95 went from ~180ms to ~420ms and p99 spiked to ~1.2s. they're seeing timeouts on synchronous tool calls. attaching a short summary and repro below.

Aisha (Support): customer payload: structured_output + function routing enabled, complex JSON schema for tool outputs (deeply nested arrays). They said it used to be fine for months, started ~2026-03-12 15:10 UTC.

Aisha (Support): repro curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/tool-run \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Extract items"}], "tool_router":true, "structured_output":{"schema":<big-schema>}}'
```

Ben (SRE): thanks. can you paste a sample response time histogram / logs? any request ids?

Aisha (Support): pasted some logs from their trace (redacted):```
[2026-03-12T15:12:03Z] request_id=rc_9a1b p95=423ms p99=1210ms route=/chat/tool-run model=rwd-3b structured_validation=on schema_size=48kb
[2026-03-12T15:12:08Z] request_id=rc_9a2c p95=401ms p99=1189ms route=/chat/tool-run model=rwd-3b structured_validation=on schema_size=48kb
```

Marta (Eng-ML): quick hypothesis: the router adds JSON schema validation (AJV) on the hot path for tool outputs. large schemas compiled per-request (or deserialized) + sync deep validation could add tens to hundreds of ms. Did the runtime deploy touch the router/validation path?

Dong (Platform): we rolled the router change yesterday to support richer structured_output metadata. the change added a validation step in the request path to enforce schema before invoking downstream tools. it was meant to avoid sending malformed payloads to customers' tool endpoints.

Ben (SRE): ok that explains timing. do we have flamegraph/profiler for a slow request?

Marta (Eng-ML): I grabbed a profile from a repro run on staging: validation took ~120-180ms in multiple samples, the rest of the pipeline stayed ~40-60ms. stack shows ajv.validateSync -> deep object traversal -> allocs. repeating for every request and for each candidate tool.

Marta (Eng-ML): other notes: some customers use large schemas (48kb example). AJV's compile step is expensive if you compile per-request; compile-once and reuse helps, but deep validation still costs CPU time. Streaming validation (schema-first streaming) can still be heavy for nested arrays.

Ben (SRE): severity = customer-impacting. Are p95/p99 regressions limited to tool-router routes? Any cross-correlation with model size?

Aisha (Support): customer says mainly when tool_router + structured_output schema present. non-tool routes unaffected.

Dong (Platform): rollback option: revert the added sync validation to async pipeline, but we need safeguards to avoid invalid tool calls. could we enqueue schema validation after response and send a warning webhook if invalid?

Marta (Eng-ML): immediate mitigations we can do today: 1) compile schemas once and cache compiled validators (AJV) keyed by schema hash. 2) add a lightweight quick-check for schema size and skip heavy validation for >32kb until async. 3) allow opt-out flag validate_schema=false in API for customers who can self-validate. 4) stream-based validation to reduce allocations.

Ben (SRE): medium term: move validation to a separate validation service with its own autoscaling and CPU pool, or run validation on background workers. that'll remove blocking from the hot inference path.

Aisha (Support): customer wants workaround now — they can toggle structured_output off but that's not ideal. can we offer an API header to disable validation per-request?

Dong (Platform): yes we can add X-Redwood-Validate: false header and a config toggle on their project. but must be gated for enterprise customers and audited. will need product signoff + docs.

Marta (Eng-ML): small patch idea: compile AJV schemas into a shared process memory on router start (or when schema first seen) and reuse validators. that'll cut compile cost out. Also set a short TTL for compiled validators to avoid memory bloat.

Ben (SRE): also add metrics: validation_latency_ms histogram, validation_failure_count, schema_size_bucket. Need these before rolling anything.

ops-bot: Canary rollback started for commit c3f9a2 on namespace=eng-runtime (initiated by @Dong).

Dong (Platform): I'm triggering a partial rollback for the sync validation change to restore p95. Rolling back the router change for canary hosts now.

Aisha (Support): great — I'll tell ACMEInc to test. suggested message: "we've identified a server-side schema validation change that increased latency for some tool-calls. we're rolling back and will provide an opt-out and long-term fixes. ETA 2 hours."

Ben (SRE): action items: 1) instrument validation latency (Ben) 2) implement compiled-validator cache (Marta) 3) add X-Redwood-Validate header + project config toggle + audit logging (Dong) 4) create async-validation design doc for platform team (Marta+Dong) 5) customer comms (Aisha).

Marta (Eng-ML): I'll open PR for AJV compile cache and a small fast-path that bails to async for schemas > 32kb. target: patch in next 24h, canary same-day.

Dong (Platform): I'll add the header and project toggle, and restrict to projects in trial mode off by default. will add audit events. target: rollout after PR review in 48h.

Ben (SRE): once metrics are in, we'll run a quick ablation test: enable compiled-cache in canary and compare p95/p99 vs rollback baseline.

Aisha (Support): final note for support playbook: when customers report p95 spikes on tool-router routes, ask for "structured_validation" status and schema_size, suggest toggle header if available, and escalate to eng if >3% error rate or p99 > 1s.

Aisha (Support): thanks all — I'll update the ticket and ping once ACME confirms after the rollback. :thumbsup:
